current_example.problem:
Find the **total** area of the shaded region that lies between the polar curves $r=2\cos(2\theta)$ and $r=1,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/7c023033b4d3e0fa6ea5a2d9866688e360b759fba6aa0a5dd6241e148d7b093d.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
Consider the rightmost pair of petals. First, we find the values of $\theta$ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ) & =1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ) & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $2\theta \in [-\pi,\pi]$:

$$
2\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{\pi}{3} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \theta= -\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{\pi}{6}
$$

To determine which is the inner function and which is the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/1dc9ce9add3d7135f69c92590ebde003d4e5ee31446d6202222ac890e2f42a9c.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=1,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=2\cos(2\theta).$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} \Big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{outer}} \big]^2 - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{inner}} \big]^2 \Big) \:\textrm{d}\theta,
$$

where

$\qquad$ $\theta_1=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}, \quad$ and $\quad \theta_2=\dfrac{\pi}{6}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}((2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))^{2}-{1}^{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(4{cos}^{2}⁡(2\theta )-1)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))-1)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(1+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\theta {|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\theta ){|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{6}))+\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{2\pi }{3}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{2\pi }{3})) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{1}{4}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =4{A}_{1}=4(\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4})=\frac{2\pi }{3}+\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
